chunks: And from him, from al-Nadhr, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a female slave who had entered into a contract of manumission (mukatabah), who died after having paid most of what was due to her, and who had given birth to a child during her period of manumission. He ruled regarding her child: 'One half of him is freed, corresponding to what was freed from her, and the other half remains in servitude, corresponding to what remained in servitude from her.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali, peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٍ: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a fixed sum to a master for freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a child born to a slave woman who dies after paying most of her manumission debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) application of the principle of proportional manumission (*mukataba*) to the offspring of a female slave who dies after settling most of her debt. It establishes that the child inherits a mixed status: half free, corresponding to the portion of the mother’s freedom already purchased, and half enslaved, corresponding to the remaining debt. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view of the child as a distinct entity whose status is derived from the mother’s partial legal standing at the time of her death.
